sentences.en: Back in August, Daily Producer Lindsey Garrison and I went to Missouri to visit the state's only remaining abortion clinic.
sentences.zh: 早在八月，我和《每日》的制片人琳赛·加里森去了密苏里州，参观了该州仅存的一家堕胎诊所。

sentences.en: Justice Kennedy had just announced he would be retiring from the Supreme Court, basically guaranteeing a more conservative court.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪大法官刚刚宣布他将从最高法院退休，这基本上保证了法院将变得更加保守。

sentences.en: The thinking was that while this might not result in Roe v.
sentences.zh: 当时的想法是，虽然这可能不会导致“罗诉韦德案”被推翻，

sentences.en: Wade being overturned, it would probably mean that red states would become more like Missouri, increasingly emboldened to limit abortion.
sentences.zh: 但这很可能意味着红州会变得越来越像密苏里州，在限制堕胎方面变得越来越大胆。

sentences.en: We wanted to see what that looked like.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看那是什么样子。

sentences.en: But it turned out that it couldn't have been worse timing for abortion to come back into the national conversation.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，堕胎问题重新回到全国讨论的焦点，时机再糟糕不过了。

sentences.en: Claire McCaskill was a Democratic senator trying desperately to keep her seat against a conservative Republican, Josh Hawley.
sentences.zh: 克莱尔·麦卡斯基尔是一位民主党参议员，正拼命试图保住她的席位，对抗保守派共和党人乔什·霍利。

sentences.en: And this was a state that had gone for Donald Trump by nearly 20 points.
sentences.zh: 而这是一个唐纳德·特朗普以近20个百分点优势胜出的州。

sentences.en: So when she lost, we knew we wanted to talk to her about what had happened and what she makes of it.
sentences.zh: 所以当她落选时，我们知道我们想和她谈谈发生了什么，以及她对此有何看法。

sentences.zh: 于是，琳赛和我上周二去了国会大厦，

sentences.en: And I want you, Senator McCaskill, to go back and remember for me what politics were like when you first started in politics in Missouri.
sentences.zh: 麦卡斯基尔参议员，我想请你回想一下，当你刚开始在密苏里州从政时，那里的政治环境是什么样的？

sentences.en: Well, it was a blurry line back then because we didn't have the sharp divisions based on cultural issues.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那时界限比较模糊，因为我们没有基于文化议题的尖锐分歧。

sentences.en: There were a whole lot of anti-choice Democrats in the Missouri legislature.
sentences.zh: 密苏里州议会里有很多反对堕胎的民主党人。

sentences.en: There were a whole lot of pro-gun Democrats in the
sentences.zh: 密苏里州议会里有很多支持拥枪的民主党人。

sentences.en: Missouri legislature.
sentences.zh: 密苏里州议会里有很多来自农村地区的民主党人。

sentences.en: There were a whole lot of rural Democrats in the Missouri legislature.
sentences.zh: 密苏里州议会里有很多来自农村地区的民主党人。

sentences.en: Kind of hard to imagine today, right?
sentences.zh: 今天很难想象，对吧？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: The Missouri legislature is dominated now by
sentences.zh: 现在的密苏里州议会主要由共和党人主导，

sentences.en: Republicans, by and large, because of the strength of the Republican Party outside of the two major urban areas.
sentences.zh: 这主要是因为共和党在两个主要城市地区之外的势力非常强大。

sentences.en: When did you start seeing that change?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候开始看到这种变化的？

sentences.en: Well, you started seeing it really during the Clinton years when you started having a lot more
sentences.zh: 嗯，你真正开始看到这种变化是在克林顿执政时期，当时出现了更多的问题，

sentences.en: issues come up, whether it was abortion or whether it was guns or whether it was gay rights.
sentences.zh: 无论是堕胎、枪支还是同性恋权利问题。

sentences.en: And so as we began to address some of the inequities in our country as a party, there were a whole lot of white
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们作为一个政党开始解决国内的一些不平等问题时，有很多白人蓝领选民，

sentences.en: working class voters, particularly in rural America, that said, well, what about me?
sentences.zh: 特别是在美国农村地区，他们说，那我们呢？

sentences.en: Hey, what about me?
sentences.zh: 嘿，那我们呢？

sentences.en: And really, that's the vein that Trump tapped into very, very effectively as a good marketer.
sentences.zh: 作为一名优秀的营销者，特朗普非常、非常有效地利用了这种情绪。

sentences.en: And how did you navigate that, Senator McCaskill?
sentences.zh: 麦卡斯基尔参议员，你是如何应对这种情况的？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, clearly not very well because I loSt. Two terMs. Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，显然应对得并不好，因为我输了。两届任期。是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, I think there's a whole bunch of voters in Missouri that don't make up their mind on party.
sentences.zh: 我认为密苏里州有一大批选民并不是根据党派来做决定的。

sentences.en: And so my goal was always to work harder than everybody else, to show up, show respect.
sentences.zh: 所以我的目标总是比别人更努力地工作，到场，表现出尊重。

sentences.en: That counts for a lot.
sentences.zh: 这很重要。

sentences.en: If we hadn't had the Kavanaugh spectacle, if Trump hadn't camped out in Missouri, I think we would have had a chance this time because we had a
sentences.zh: 如果我们没有经历卡瓦诺那场闹剧，如果特朗普没有驻扎在密苏里州，我想我们这次是有机会的，因为我们这边有很多动力，而他们当时并没有那么热情。

sentences.en: lot of motivation on our side and they weren't that enthusiastic.
sentences.zh: 而且我强调了议题。

sentences.en: And I stressed issues.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的背景是审计员和检察官。

sentences.en: You know, my background was an auditor and a prosecutor.
sentences.zh: 谁不想要安全的街道，谁不希望我们监管好纳税人的钱呢？

sentences.en: Well, who doesn't want safe streets and who doesn't want us to keep track of taxpayer money?
sentences.zh: 所以我在这方面做了大量工作。

sentences.en: So I did an awful lot of work in those buckets.
sentences.zh: 这吸引了我们州那些无法按党派划分的选民。

sentences.en: And that appeals to those voters that are not identifiable by party in our state.
sentences.zh: 我以为我能从中间派那里争取到足够的支持，从而在这次选举中胜出。

sentences.en: And I thought I could get enough out of that middle to get it across the finish line this time.
sentences.zh: 但我以为我能从中间派那里争取到足够的支持，从而在这次选举中胜出。

sentences.en: But Caravan, Kavanaugh, and Trump camping out were the three things that really amped up their side and ultimately caused the defeat.
sentences.zh: 但是大篷车移民、卡瓦诺事件以及特朗普的驻扎，这三件事真正激怒了对方，最终导致了我的失败。

sentences.en: And part of this is journalism.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分原因是新闻业。

sentences.en: I think journalism has really made this a much more difficult job.
sentences.zh: 我认为新闻业确实让这份工作变得困难多了。

sentences.en: Now everyone can pick a network for affirmation and just kind of stew in their own juices.
sentences.zh: 现在每个人都可以选择一个频道来寻求认同，然后沉浸在自己的偏见中。

sentences.en: You have places where you can find an echo chamber.
sentences.zh: 你可以在某些地方找到回声室。

sentences.en: And that is a problem.
sentences.zh: 这是一个问题。

sentences.en: The broader public conversation is broken down.
sentences.zh: 更广泛的公共对话已经破裂了。

sentences.en: It's broken down.
sentences.zh: 它已经破裂了。

sentences.en: So my colleagues that are from bright blue places, they want to make sure that they're appealing to the base of the party almost exclusively.
sentences.zh: 所以，来自深蓝地区的同事们，他们几乎只想着如何吸引本党的基本盘。

sentences.en: My colleagues are from bright red places, ditto.
sentences.zh: 来自深红地区的同事们也是如此。

sentences.en: People that are from states like mine still understand that the two sides yelling at each other or yelling about things that are not going to get done only increases cynicism.
sentences.zh: 来自像我这样州的人仍然明白，双方互相叫嚷，或者为那些无法解决的事情争吵，只会增加愤世嫉俗的情绪。

sentences.en: If we don't pull people into the middle, shave off the edges and find something we can agree on, we're never going to make any progress, especially on the tough stuff.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不把人们拉向中间，消除极端，找到我们可以达成共识的东西，我们就永远无法取得任何进展，尤其是在棘手的问题上。

sentences.en: I mean, that's where compromise is going to have to happen.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是必须进行妥协的地方。

sentences.en: And everyone is scared to death to compromise.
sentences.zh: 而每个人都害怕妥协。

sentences.en: So I started to understand the politics of Missouri this summer because Brett Kavanaugh had just been
sentences.zh: 所以今年夏天我开始理解密苏里州的政治，因为布雷特·卡瓦诺刚刚被提名进入最高法院，我们想去一个已经对堕胎准入有相当多限制的州。

sentences.en: nominated to the Supreme Court and we wanted to go to a state that had already pretty restricted access.
sentences.zh: 所以密苏里州实际上只有一个诊所。

sentences.en: So Missouri effectively only had one clinic.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 我本以为该州唯一的民主党参议员会为此而战，会站在前线，你知道，支持这种支持堕胎选择的立场。

sentences.en: And I was expecting to find the state's one Democratic senator really be fighting for this, kind of be on the barricades about it, you know, be supporting this pro-choice position.
sentences.zh: 我本以为该州唯一的民主党参议员会为此而战，会站在前线，你知道，支持这种支持堕胎选择的立场。

sentences.en: And I was pretty surprised that you didn't.
sentences.zh: 但我很惊讶你没有这样做。

sentences.en: You weren't.
sentences.zh: 你没有。

sentences.en: You were quiet on it.
sentences.zh: 你对此保持沉默。

sentences.en: And I talked to a lot of Democrats who were really upset about that.
sentences.zh: 我和许多对此感到非常不满的民主党人谈过。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering if you understand why.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是否明白为什么。

sentences.en: Well, no, not really.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不，并不明白。

sentences.en: My voting record is perfect.
sentences.zh: 我的投票记录是完美的。

sentences.en: I think I have very been clear about my position.
sentences.zh: 我认为我已经非常清楚地表明了我的立场。

sentences.en: I think the people you talk to, I'm willing to bet, I could probably name three or four of them,
sentences.zh: 我敢打赌，你谈到的那些人——我大概能说出其中三四个人的名字——

sentences.en: are young women who have not spent any time outside of the group of people that agree with them.
sentences.zh: 都是些年轻女性，她们除了和自己意见一致的人群外，没有花任何时间去接触其他人。

sentences.en: They probably don't understand that Trump's success had a whole lot to do with economic angSt.
sentences.zh: 她们可能不明白特朗普的成功与经济焦虑有很大关系。

sentences.en: And I knew that if I ignored the meat and potatoes of this election, which was all about, will people be able to get health care?
sentences.zh: 我知道，如果我忽视了这次选举的实质问题，也就是人们是否能获得医疗保健，

sentences.en: Can they afford health care?
sentences.zh: 他们是否负担得起医疗保健？

sentences.en: What about the price of prescription drugs?
sentences.zh: 处方药的价格怎么办？

sentences.en: These were all things that everybody in Missouri, when I'd go out to all the town halls, everybody would shake their heads.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我在密苏里州参加所有市政厅会议时，每个人都会点头表示关注的问题。

sentences.en: I think those people who were upset that I wasn't talking about it, shame on them if they don't know my voting record.
sentences.zh: 我认为那些因为我没有谈论这个问题而感到不满的人，如果她们不了解我的投票记录，那是她们的耻辱。

sentences.en: And shame on them that they're not working as hard as they can for me and not trashing me because of my voting record in a hard state.
sentences.zh: 如果她们不尽其所能为我工作，反而因为我在一个艰难的州里的投票记录而抨击我，那是她们的耻辱。

sentences.en: What did you want to say to them?
sentences.zh: 你想对她们说什么？

sentences.en: Shut up.
sentences.zh: 闭嘴。

sentences.en: You know, really?
sentences.zh: 你知道，真的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, this is hard.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很难。

sentences.en: It can have been one thing if I'd ever wavered.
sentences.zh: 如果我曾经动摇过，那是一回事。

sentences.en: But I've had to take a lot of tough votes over the years on this issue.
sentences.zh: 但多年来，在这个问题上，我不得不投下许多艰难的票。

sentences.en: I have been standing in the breach for women's rights as it relates to reproductive freedom for all of my adult life.
sentences.zh: 我成年后的整个人生都在为女性在生殖自由方面的权利而战。

sentences.en: And the fact that these young women didn't realize that and just be quiet, roll up their sleeves and work their ass off for me was beyond irritating.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这些年轻女性没有意识到这一点，她们应该保持安静，卷起袖子，为我拼命工作，而不是因为这个而指责我，这简直让人无法忍受。

sentences.en: Can you tell?
sentences.zh: 你能看出来吗？

sentences.en: Well, I can tell.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我看得出来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So, you know, rather than go, oh, you know, to the New York Times podcast, you know, she's not doing enough.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，与其去《纽约时报》播客上说，哦，你知道，她做得不够。

sentences.en: She's not talking about it enough.
sentences.zh: 她谈论得不够多。

sentences.en: Well, get out there and work and reelect her and quit complaining because Josh Hawley thinks the morning after pill should be illegal.
sentences.zh: 好吧，走出去工作，重新选举她，别再抱怨了，因为乔什·霍利认为事后避孕药应该是非法的。

sentences.en: He has said publicly he wants to overturn Roe v.
sentences.zh: 他公开表示他想推翻“罗诉韦德案”。

sentences.en: Wade.
So to me, there was a huge difference in the two of us.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，我们两人之间有巨大的差异。

sentences.en: And the fact they didn't appreciate that difference and they were willing to be critical that I wasn't talking about it enough.
sentences.zh: 而她们没有意识到这种差异，并且愿意因为我谈论得不够多而批评我，这让我感到遗憾。

sentences.en: Dumb.
sentences.zh: 愚蠢。

sentences.en: It wasn't that I was changing my position on the issue.
sentences.zh: 并不是我改变了在这个问题上的立场。

sentences.en: It was it was not an issue that was going to bring me more votes.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是一个能为我带来更多选票的议题。

sentences.en: So effectively, do you want to win or do you want to feel morally pure?
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上，你是想赢，还是想在道德上保持纯洁？

sentences.en: Yeah, I want to I want to win so that I can be there to vote the right way on issues that really matter to those young women and to me.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想赢，这样我就能在那儿投票，在那些对年轻女性和我自己真正重要的问题上做出正确的选择。

sentences.en: And it's not like these young women.
sentences.zh: 而且这并不是说这些年轻女性不好。

sentences.en: I get it.
sentences.zh: 我明白。

sentences.en: And I love their passion.
sentences.zh: 我热爱她们的热情。

sentences.en: And I love it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢。

sentences.en: They're out there working on this.
sentences.zh: 她们在外面为此奔走努力。

sentences.en: But they need to remember who their friends are and not make it more difficult for their friends.
sentences.zh: 但她们需要记住谁是她们的朋友，不要让她们的朋友处境更艰难。

sentences.en: So when the assault allegations came out against Brett Kavanaugh, were you thinking, oh, shit, there goes all my work at keeping things local.
sentences.zh: 那么，当针对布雷特·卡瓦诺的性侵指控出现时，你有没有想过，“糟了，我为保持地方性所做的一切努力都白费了”？

sentences.en: You were trying to walk that line and not be dragged into this kind of vortex of national politics.
sentences.zh: 你当时试图走那条中间路线，不想被卷入这种全国性政治的漩涡中。

sentences.en: Well, frankly, the oh, shit moment was when Kennedy resigned.
sentences.zh: 嗯，坦白说，那个“糟了”的时刻是肯尼迪大法官辞职的时候。

sentences.en: Paint that picture.
sentences.zh: 描述一下当时的场景吧。

sentences.en: I was actually in my office and I was actually having a picture taken for a magazine article.
sentences.zh: 我当时其实在办公室里，正在为一篇杂志文章拍照。

sentences.en: And they had me by a window in my office.
sentences.zh: 他们让我站在办公室的窗边。

sentences.en: It's right by the door that leads to my staff.
sentences.zh: 就在通往我员工办公区的门边。

sentences.en: And it was really quiet.
sentences.zh: 当时非常安静。

sentences.en: And the picture was clicking.
sentences.zh: 相机快门声咔哒咔哒响着。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, this voice shouted out, oh, shit.
sentences.zh: 突然，一个声音大喊道：“糟了！”

sentences.en: I thought, oh, God, one of my staff members is back there.
sentences.zh: 我心想，天哪，是我的一位员工在后面。

sentences.en: And I was a little embarrassed.
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得有点尴尬。

sentences.en: And so the photographer left and I opened the door.
sentences.zh: 于是摄影师离开了，我打开了门。

sentences.en: I go, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 我问：“怎么了？”

sentences.en: And I looked at the screen.
sentences.zh: 我看向屏幕。

sentences.en: And it was Kennedy is retiring.
sentences.zh: 上面写着：肯尼迪即将退休。

sentences.en: And so everybody in my office knew this was going to be a challenge because it was going to bring to the forefront issues that really divide us.
sentences.zh: 我办公室里的每个人都知道这将是一个挑战，因为它会把那些真正让我们分裂的问题推到风口浪尖。

sentences.en: So that's when I knew it was going to be a struggle.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时就知道这将是一场苦战。

sentences.en: And then, as it turned out, it was even worse than I thought it might be before it was all over.
sentences.zh: 结果正如所料，在一切结束之前，情况比我预想的还要糟糕。

sentences.en: I still think I could have survived had perhaps been handled slightly differently.
sentences.zh: 我仍然认为，如果处理方式稍有不同，我本可以挺过来的。

sentences.en: So do you think the Democrats messed that up?
sentences.zh: 所以你认为民主党人把这件事搞砸了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In what way?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: I think when the letter was received by the Judiciary Committee, it was imperative that even though the woman wanted confidentiality, the FBI is capable of confidentiality.
sentences.zh: 我认为当司法委员会收到那封信时，即使那位女士想要保密，联邦调查局也有能力处理保密事宜，这至关重要。

sentences.en: And had it been turned over right away, they could not have ever said that this was an 11th hour kneecap.
sentences.zh: 如果当时立即移交，他们就永远无法说这是“最后一刻的暗算”。

sentences.en: It looked like this was political on the part of the Democrats doing this at the very end.
sentences.zh: 这看起来像是民主党人在最后时刻搞的政治动作。

sentences.en: And appearances matter more than substance sometimes, especially in the closing weeks of a contested election in a pretty red place.
sentences.zh: 有时候表象比实质更重要，尤其是在一个相当保守的选区，在竞选的最后几周。

sentences.en: When did you realize that you were going to lose?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候意识到自己要输了的？

sentences.en: So I knew the last three weeks that if we won, it was going to be incredibly close.
sentences.zh: 最后三周我就知道，如果我们赢了，那也会赢得非常惊险。

sentences.en: And I knew the chances were good that we wouldn't win.
sentences.zh: 而且我知道我们很可能赢不了。

sentences.en: Do you feel that the Kavanaugh hearing was pretty much responsible for your loss?
sentences.zh: 你觉得卡瓦诺的听证会很大程度上导致了你的失败吗？

sentences.en: That, along with the caravan optics and Trump camping out in Missouri, those three things together really pumped up the other side.
sentences.zh: 那件事，加上移民大篷车的舆论，还有特朗普在密苏里州的造势，这三件事加在一起确实极大地鼓舞了对方阵营。

sentences.en: It got people who maybe don't vote that frequently, and certainly not in a midterm, but like are all down with Donald Trump and the idea of giving
sentences.zh: 它让那些平时不怎么投票，当然更不会在期中选举投票的人，但他们完全支持唐纳德·特朗普，支持那种向建制派竖中指的想法，

sentences.en: the finger to the establishment, it got them off the couch.
sentences.zh: 这让他们走出了家门。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《时报》一个月，而且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间去探索付费墙后的内容，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，免费获取30天的访问权限。

sentences.en: It did feel like there was quite a real sort of changing of the guards, and there was maybe some
sentences.zh: 确实感觉有一种真正的“换岗”感，而且可能传达出某种信息，

sentences.en: sort of a message in it that, you know, you lost in Missouri, Joe Donnelly lost in Indiana, Heidi Heitkamp lost in North Dakota.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你在密苏里州输了，乔·唐纳利在印第安纳州输了，海蒂·海特坎普在北达科他州输了。

sentences.en: You guys were the ones that were really trying really hard to connect to rural voters.
sentences.zh: 你们这些人真的是在非常努力地与农村选民建立联系。

sentences.en: I mean, you did, you know, you were really, really, really strong candidates who'd won before, and you all loSt.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你们确实是，你们是非常、非常、非常强大的候选人，以前都赢过，但你们都输了。

sentences.en: I mean, what does that say about where we are right now in politics?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这说明了我们现在的政治处于什么境地？

sentences.en: Is the middle gone?
sentences.zh: 中间派消失了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, can a Democrat win in a red state?
sentences.zh: 我是说，民主党人能在红色州获胜吗？

sentences.en: Well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，可以。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, Kyrsten Sinema won a seat in the Senate in Arizona in a state that hadn't elected Democrat in decades.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我是说，克里斯滕·西内马在亚利桑那州赢得了一个参议院席位，那个州几十年来都没有选出过民主党人。

sentences.en: People, I think, you know, maybe 10 minutes ago would have called Arizona red.
sentences.zh: 我想，人们可能在10分钟前还会称亚利桑那州为红色州。

sentences.en: I think this is a Trump-inspired pendulum swing to the right, a little bit of a hangover from the Obama years
sentences.zh: 我认为这是特朗普引发的钟摆向右摆动，是奥巴马时代留下的某种后遗症，

sentences.en: in areas of our country that many of those voters voted for Obama, but nothing changed for them.
sentences.zh: 在我们国家的某些地区，许多选民曾投票给奥巴马，但他们的生活没有任何改变。

sentences.en: They're still not doing as well as their parents did.
sentences.zh: 他们现在的生活依然不如他们的父母。

sentences.en: They still can't afford to retire.
sentences.zh: 他们依然负担不起退休费用。

sentences.en: They still lost their job at the car plant and are working for half the money and without the benefits than they were when the car plant was open.
sentences.zh: 他们依然失去了汽车厂的工作，拿着比工厂开工时少一半的工资，而且没有福利。

sentences.en: I got those in my state.
sentences.zh: 我的州里也有这样的人。

sentences.en: I know Joe Donnelly has those people in his state.
sentences.zh: 我知道乔·唐纳利在他们的州也有这样的人。

sentences.en: And it was not long enough in the Trump administration for them to be as cynical about him as they became about Obama.
sentences.zh: 而且特朗普政府执政的时间还不够长，让他们像对奥巴马那样对他感到愤世嫉俗。

sentences.en: And why, Senator, do you think that people have not really been moved when it turns out that the policies aren't so great or it's kind of not what it is?
sentences.zh: 那么参议员，你认为为什么当事实证明政策并不那么好，或者情况并非如此时，人们并没有真正被触动？

sentences.en: Because they wanted to give him time.
sentences.zh: 因为他们想给他时间。

sentences.en: It's like the tariffs.
sentences.zh: 就像关税一样。

sentences.en: How do you put tariffs on soybeans, the most important crop in Missouri, without there being a huge fallout?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能在密苏里州最重要的农作物大豆上加征关税，而不产生巨大的后果呢？

sentences.en: Well, because they believe him that, just give me time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为他们相信他，相信“再给我一点时间”。

sentences.en: It's going to be better.
sentences.zh: 情况会好转的。

sentences.en: You know, he knows what he's doing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: He's a really good businessman.
sentences.zh: 他是个非常优秀的商人。

sentences.en: He knows how to negotiate.
sentences.zh: 他懂得如何谈判。

sentences.en: Slowly but surely, they're beginning to realize, well, maybe, just maybe the emperor doesn't wear any clothes.
sentences.zh: 慢慢地，他们开始意识到，好吧，也许，仅仅是也许，皇帝其实没穿衣服。

sentences.en: But not yet.
sentences.zh: 但现在还不是时候。

sentences.en: Not yet.
sentences.zh: 还没到那时候。

sentences.en: More importantly, maybe, is the question, what does it do for our candidates running for president against him?
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，也许问题在于，这对我们竞选总统的候选人有什么影响？

sentences.en: And how do we nominate someone who can compete in states like Wisconsin, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Florida, and Ohio, even if they can't win in states like Indiana and Missouri?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何提名一个能在威斯康星州、密歇根州、宾夕法尼亚州、佛罗里达州和俄亥俄州竞争的人，即使他们无法在印第安纳州和密苏里州获胜？

sentences.en: Because the next step for the pendulum swinging back is for Donald Trump to be defeated in 2020.
sentences.zh: 因为钟摆回摆的下一步，就是让唐纳德·特朗普在2020年被击败。

sentences.en: So I just want to make sure that all the people who have been elected to Congress from very blue districts listen to the people who were elected from Congress that replaced Republicans,
sentences.zh: 所以我只是想确保所有从深蓝选区当选国会议员的人，能听听那些取代共和党人当选国会议员的人的意见，

sentences.en: not defeated Democrats in primaries, if you know who I mean.
sentences.zh: 而不是那些在初选中击败民主党人的人，如果你明白我的意思的话。

sentences.en: Well, what's her name everybody's fascinated with from New York?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那个来自纽约的、大家都着迷的女人叫什么名字？

sentences.en: Cortez.
sentences.zh: 科尔特斯。

sentences.en: I mean, God love her, but I hope she listens to people who defeated Republicans, because it's the people who defeated Republicans in this election that we need to be emulating,
sentences.zh: 我是说，上帝保佑她，但我希望她能听听那些击败了共和党人的人的意见，因为正是这次选举中击败共和党人的人，才是我们需要效仿的对象，

sentences.en: not the people who defeated Democrats in primaries.
sentences.zh: 而不是那些在初选中击败民主党人的人。

sentences.en: And that goes back to the kind of pure than pure base that doesn't understand the broader picture.
sentences.zh: 这又回到了那种“比纯洁更纯洁”的基层，他们不了解大局。

sentences.en: Well, they may understand it, but they are so passionate about their beliefs, they feel that if everybody would just be more pure, more people would come to the cause.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们可能了解，但他们对自己的信仰如此充满热情，他们觉得如果每个人都能更纯洁一点，就会有更多人加入他们的事业。

sentences.en: And many of them have not been in a place where the math is unforgiving to that concept.
sentences.zh: 而且他们中的许多人还没有经历过那种对这一概念毫不留情的现实考验。

sentences.en: And so I just want to make sure that we don't make a mistake and go so far to the left in nominating a candidate that we lose all those white working class voters that had been a huge part of our party decades ago.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是想确保我们不会犯错，在提名候选人时走得太左，以至于失去了几十年来一直是我们党重要组成部分的那些白人蓝领选民。

sentences.en: While we maintain great enthusiasm by young people, we need somebody who can bridge that divide.
sentences.zh: 在保持年轻人巨大热情的同时，我们需要一个能够弥合这种分歧的人。

sentences.en: So we have an opportunity in 2020, as long as we don't go so far off the left side of the earth, that we alienate those people that when they hear the word free college,
sentences.zh: 所以我们在2020年有机会，只要我们不走得太偏左，以至于疏远了那些人——当他们听到“免费大学”这个词时，

sentences.en: they hear that phrase, they think, oh, look, they're giving away something to other people besides me again.
sentences.zh: 他们听到这个短语，就会想：“噢，看，他们又在给除了我以外的其他人发福利了。”

sentences.en: I had to earn mine.
sentences.zh: 我的是靠自己挣来的。

sentences.en: Why aren't they having to earn theirs?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们不用靠自己挣？

sentences.en: That thing is real.
sentences.zh: 这种想法是真实存在的。

sentences.en: Sometimes going too far, we turn off people and make election victories impossible.
sentences.zh: 有时候走得太远，我们会让人们反感，导致选举胜利变得不可能。

sentences.en: I'll tell you a true story.
sentences.zh: 我给你讲个真实的故事。

sentences.en: I'm at a gas station in Kingdom City, which is a stop in the highway.
sentences.zh: 我在王国城的一个加油站，那是高速公路上的一个停靠点。

sentences.en: And this is about a month after President Trump was inaugurated.
sentences.zh: 那是在特朗普总统就职大约一个月后。

sentences.en: And there was a good old boy over by the gas pumps.
sentences.zh: 加油泵旁边有个老派的家伙。

sentences.en: And he said, hey, you, hey, you, which in Missouri is senator, senator.
sentences.zh: 他说：“嘿，你，嘿，你。”在密苏里州，这就是指“参议员，参议员”。

sentences.en: So I walked over and I said, what can I do for you, sir?
sentences.zh: 所以我走过去说：“先生，我能为您做些什么吗？”

sentences.en: And he started shaking his finger in my face.
sentences.zh: 他开始指着我的脸摇手指。

sentences.en: He said, I voted for you before and I may vote for you again.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我以前投过你的票，我可能还会再投给你。”

sentences.en: But I want you to know why I didn't vote for her, Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: “但我得让你知道我为什么没投给她，希拉里·克林顿。”

sentences.en: I knew she cared about women.
sentences.zh: “我知道她关心女性。”

sentences.en: I knew she cared about MusliMs.
sentences.zh: “我知道她关心穆斯林。”

sentences.en: I knew she cared about Mexicans.
sentences.zh: “我知道她关心墨西哥人。”

sentences.en: I knew she cared about homosexuals.
sentences.zh: “我知道她关心同性恋者。”

sentences.en: I really knew she, you know, really cared a lot about black people.
sentences.zh: “我确实知道她，你知道，真的很关心黑人。”

sentences.en: But I was pretty sure she didn't give a shit about me.
sentences.zh: “但我很确定她根本不在乎我。”

sentences.en: So if we center on economics and how people are frustrated about their economic situation, we will have a great deal more success.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们专注于经济，以及人们对经济状况的挫败感，我们将取得更大的成功。

sentences.en: And not that we don't want to be a party of opportunity and equality.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说我们不想成为一个代表机会和平等的政党。

sentences.en: Of course we do.
sentences.zh: 我们当然想。

sentences.en: Of course we do.
sentences.zh: 我们当然想。

sentences.en: But we've got to make sure that in that we don't miss the fact that a rural family living on the edge of poverty is no different than an urban family living on the edge of poverty.
sentences.zh: 但我们必须确保，在这样做的时候，我们不会忽略一个事实：生活在贫困边缘的农村家庭与生活在贫困边缘的城市家庭没有什么不同。

sentences.en: And that's what's happened is many people in rural Missouri don't think we give a shit about them.
sentences.zh: 而现在发生的事情是，密苏里州农村地区的许多人认为我们根本不在乎他们。

sentences.en: That there's this contempt.
sentences.zh: 认为我们对他们有一种轻蔑。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that we think we're better than them, smarter than them, and don't get them.
sentences.zh: 认为我们觉得自己比他们优越，比他们聪明，而且不理解他们。

sentences.en: That is part of the Democratic Party's problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是民主党问题的一部分。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it did really strike us that, you know, particularly with, I mean, the abortion politics in Missouri was one example, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这确实让我们印象深刻，你知道，特别是，我是说，密苏里州的堕胎政治就是一个例子，对吧？

sentences.en: But it felt like, you know, these two extremes are kind of what makes up everyday politics
sentences.zh: 但感觉就像，你知道，这两个极端构成了日常政治，

sentences.en: when most people are sort of watching that on their television and just turning away in disguSt.
sentences.zh: 而大多数人只是在电视上看着这些，然后厌恶地转过头去。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The noise in the system is being generated by the ins, not by the middle.
sentences.zh: 系统中的噪音是由极端分子制造的，而不是由中间派制造的。

sentences.en: Nobody calls my office to say, I'm calling to ask Senator McCaskill to compromise.
sentences.zh: 没有人打电话给我的办公室说：“我打电话是请求麦卡斯基尔参议员妥协的。”

sentences.en: No one writes a letter saying, you know, can't you find the middle?
sentences.zh: 没有人写信说：“你知道，难道你们不能找到中间立场吗？”

sentences.en: Can't you?
sentences.zh: “难道不能吗？”

sentences.en: But they still expect us to get things done.

sentences.en: In a surprise move on Wednesday, President Trump ordered that all 2,000 U.S.
sentences.zh: 周三，特朗普总统出人意料地命令将所有2000名美国地面部队在30天内撤出叙利亚，

sentences.en: ground troops in Syria be withdrawn within 30 days, despite pressure from his own generals to keep a military presence there.
sentences.zh: 尽管他自己的将军们施压要求保持在那里的军事存在。

sentences.en: In a tweet explaining the decision, Trump declared that the original mission of putting troops
sentences.zh: 在解释这一决定的推文中，特朗普宣称将部队派往叙利亚以击败“伊斯兰国”的最初任务已经完成，

sentences.en: in Syria to defeat ISIS has been completed, a conclusion his own military and diplomatic staff have rejected in recent public remarks.
sentences.zh: 这一结论遭到了他自己的军事和外交人员在最近公开言论中的反驳。

sentences.en: Well, there'll be multiple objectives in Syria.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在叙利亚会有多个目标。

sentences.en: So the military objective, very clearly, the military objective is the enduring defeat of ISIS.
sentences.zh: 所以军事目标，非常明确，军事目标是持久地击败“伊斯兰国”。

sentences.en: And if we've learned one thing over the years, enduring defeat of a group like this means you can't just defeat their physical space and then leave.
sentences.zh: 如果我们这些年来学到了一件事，那就是持久地击败这样一个组织，意味着你不能仅仅击败他们的物理空间然后就离开。

sentences.en: You have to make sure that the internal security forces are in place to ensure that those security gains are enduring.
sentences.zh: 你必须确保内部安全部队到位，以确保这些安全成果是持久的。
